article.title: The Economics of Food Waste Across Supply Chains

paragraphs.en: Food waste is frequently described as a problem of individual behavior, such as buying too much or forgetting leftovers. Yet a substantial share of the problem emerges before food reaches a household. Farms, processors, distributors, supermarkets, restaurants, and consumers make decisions under different economic incentives. A product may be discarded because it is damaged, because demand was overestimated, or because the cost of handling it exceeds its expected selling price. These decisions can be rational for individual businesses while creating undesirable outcomes for society. Understanding the economics of food waste requires tracing both physical products and financial incentives across the supply chain.
paragraphs.zh: 食物浪費常被描述成個人買太多或忘記吃剩菜，但大量問題在食品到達家庭前就出現。農場、加工商、物流商、超市、餐廳與消費者面對不同經濟誘因。商品可能因受損、需求高估或處理成本超過預期售價而被丟棄。這些決策對個別企業可能合理，對社會卻造成不理想結果。理解食物浪費經濟學需要追蹤供應鏈中的實物流動與財務誘因。
paragraphs.ja: 食品ロスは家庭の買い過ぎだけでなく、農場、加工、物流、小売、飲食店でも発生します。傷みや需要予測の誤り、処理費用の高さによって廃棄されることがあります。個別企業には合理的でも社会全体には望ましくない結果になり得ます。

paragraphs.en: At the farm level, growers face uncertain weather, yields, and market prices. Harvesting and transporting produce require labor and equipment. If market prices collapse, leaving some crops unharvested may cost less than collecting and shipping them. Buyers may also reject products that fail cosmetic standards even when they remain edible. Uniform size and appearance can simplify packaging, display, and consumer expectations, but strict standards can reduce the market for irregular produce. Solutions such as alternative sales channels or processing may help, although they introduce their own costs. The economic challenge is to make recovery worthwhile without pretending that every crop can be sold profitably.
paragraphs.zh: 農場面臨天氣、產量與市價不確定性。採收運輸需要勞力設備，若價格崩跌，不採收可能比收成運送便宜。買方也可能拒收外觀不符合標準、但仍可食用的農產品。統一大小外觀方便包裝陳列及符合消費者期待，但過嚴標準縮小不規則農產的市場。替代銷售通路或加工可能有幫助，但也有成本。挑戰是讓回收利用具有經濟價值，而非假設每種作物都能獲利出售。
paragraphs.ja: 農家は天候、収量、市場価格の不確実性に直面します。価格が低いと収穫費用を回収できず、作物を残す場合があります。外見の規格も販売を制限します。加工や別販路は有効でも費用がかかります。

paragraphs.en: Retailers manage a different trade-off. Empty shelves disappoint shoppers and can drive them to competitors, so stores often keep more inventory than they expect to sell. However, perishable products lose value as their remaining shelf life shortens. Forecasting errors become especially costly when demand changes suddenly because of weather, holidays, or local events. Better data and inventory systems can reduce uncertainty, but no prediction is perfect. A store must balance the cost of stockouts against the cost of unsold food. The optimal inventory level for private profit may not minimize waste, particularly when disposal imposes costs that the business does not fully bear.
paragraphs.zh: 零售商面對另一種取捨。空貨架會讓顧客失望並轉向競爭者，因此商店常備比預期銷量更多的庫存。但易腐食品的剩餘保鮮期越短，價值越低。天氣、節日或地方活動使需求突然改變時，預測錯誤成本更高。更好的資料與庫存系統能降低不確定性，卻無法完美預測。商店必須平衡缺貨與滯銷成本。私人利潤最適庫存未必讓浪費最少，尤其處置成本未完全由企業負擔時。
paragraphs.ja: 小売店は欠品を避けるため在庫を多めに持ちますが、生鮮食品は時間とともに価値が下がります。天候や行事で需要が変わると予測誤差が増えます。利益に最適な在庫量が廃棄最小とは限りません。

paragraphs.en: Dynamic pricing offers one possible response. A supermarket may reduce the price of products approaching their recommended selling period, encouraging customers to purchase them before they lose quality. Such discounts can recover revenue and prevent waste, but timing matters. If shoppers expect deep discounts every evening, some may delay purchases, potentially reducing full-price sales. Staff also need systems to identify eligible products and update labels accurately. Digital tools can automate parts of this process, although implementation costs and fairness concerns remain. Pricing is therefore a useful instrument, not a complete solution to the wider problem.
paragraphs.zh: 動態定價是可能的對策。超市可降低接近建議販售期限商品的價格，鼓勵顧客在品質下降前購買。折扣可回收收入並減少浪費，但時機很重要。若消費者預期每天傍晚都有大折扣，可能延後購買，影響原價銷售。員工也需要系統辨識商品並正確改標。數位工具能自動化部分流程，但有導入成本及公平性疑慮。定價是有用工具，不是整體問題的完整答案。
paragraphs.ja: 期限が近い商品を値下げする動的価格設定は廃棄削減に役立ちます。ただし消費者が割引を待つようになると通常価格の売上に影響します。ラベル管理やシステム導入にも費用がかかります。

paragraphs.en: Food donation is often proposed as a way to connect surplus with people who need assistance. In practice, donated food must still be safe, collected, sorted, stored, and transported. A charity may lack refrigeration or volunteers at the precise time surplus becomes available. Liability rules, labeling requirements, and coordination between organizations can influence whether donation is feasible. Financial support for logistics may be more effective than simply asking businesses to donate more. Nevertheless, donation should not be treated as a substitute for reliable food assistance or as an excuse for routinely producing excessive surplus. Prevention and redistribution serve related but different purposes.
paragraphs.zh: 食品捐贈常被視為把剩餘食品連結到需要援助者的方法，但捐贈品仍須安全、收集、分類、儲藏與運送。慈善組織可能恰好缺冷藏設備或志工。責任規則、標示要求與機構協調都影響可行性。資助物流可能比單純要求企業多捐更有效。然而捐贈不能取代可靠的食品援助，也不應成為持續過量生產的藉口。預防與重新分配是相關但不同的目的。
paragraphs.ja: 寄付食品にも安全確認、仕分け、保管、輸送が必要です。支援団体の冷蔵設備や人手が不足する場合もあります。物流支援は重要ですが、寄付は過剰生産を正当化するものではありません。

paragraphs.en: External costs complicate the calculation. Producing food uses land, water, fertilizer, energy, and labor. When edible products are discarded, some of those resources have been used without delivering their intended nutritional benefit. Disposal can also generate greenhouse gas emissions, particularly when organic waste decomposes under conditions that produce methane. Individual businesses may not pay the full environmental cost associated with these effects. Policies such as landfill charges, separate collection, improved measurement, or support for prevention may help align private incentives with social objectives. However, poorly designed rules can increase costs or encourage misleading reporting.
paragraphs.zh: 外部成本使計算更複雜。生產食品使用土地、水、肥料、能源與勞力。可食用食品被丟棄時，部分資源消耗未帶來預期營養效益。廢棄物處理也可能產生溫室氣體，尤其有機物在產生甲烷的環境下分解。企業未必負擔完整環境成本。掩埋費、分類回收、改善量測及預防支援等政策可能使私人誘因更接近社會目標，但設計不良也可能增加成本或誘發不實報告。
paragraphs.ja: 食品生産には土地、水、肥料、エネルギーが使われます。廃棄は資源の損失となり、処理時にメタンなどの排出も生じます。企業が環境費用をすべて負担するとは限らず、制度設計が重要です。

paragraphs.en: Measurement is harder than counting discarded kilograms. Food losses differ in nutritional value, environmental impact, and recoverability. A kilogram of spoiled vegetables is not economically identical to a kilogram of discarded meat, and neither should automatically be valued only by retail price. Analysts need consistent definitions distinguishing edible surplus, unavoidable inedible parts, and products that became unsafe. Data collection must also account for what would have happened without an intervention. If a retailer reports less waste after transferring surplus to another organization, the food has not necessarily been consumed. Evaluating outcomes requires tracking the full chain rather than shifting waste between participants.
paragraphs.zh: 量測比計算丟掉幾公斤更困難。不同食品的營養價值、環境影響與可回收性不同，一公斤壞蔬菜與一公斤丟棄肉品不能只按零售價比較。分析者需要一致定義，區分可食用剩餘、不可避免的不可食部分及已不安全的商品。資料收集也須考慮沒有措施時會發生什麼。如果零售商把剩餘品移交其他機構後報告浪費減少，不代表食物真的被吃掉。評估應追蹤整條鏈，而非把浪費轉移給別人。
paragraphs.ja: 廃棄重量だけでは栄養価や環境負荷を測れません。可食部分と不可食部分、安全性を失った食品を区別します。別組織へ移しただけでは消費されたとは限らず、流れ全体の追跡が必要です。

paragraphs.en: Consumer behavior adds further complexity. Larger packages can lower the price per unit while increasing the risk that a household cannot finish the contents. Promotions that encourage multiple purchases may boost short-term sales but lead to waste at home. Confusion between quality-related date labels and safety-related expiration instructions can cause premature disposal. Public education may improve decisions, but information alone is insufficient when households face limited storage space, unpredictable schedules, or low incomes. Practical interventions include clearer labels, flexible package sizes, meal planning tools, and food storage guidance. Their effectiveness should be evaluated rather than assumed.
paragraphs.zh: 消費者行為又增加複雜性。大包裝可降低單位價格，卻增加家庭吃不完的風險；多件促銷可提高短期銷售，但可能讓家中浪費增加。混淆品質日期標示與安全期限指示，也可能過早丟棄食品。教育有幫助，但對儲藏空間不足、行程不穩定或低所得家庭而言，資訊本身不夠。清楚標示、彈性包裝、餐食規劃與保存指引都是可能措施，仍須評估成效。
paragraphs.ja: 大容量包装やまとめ買いは単価を下げますが、家庭で食べ切れないリスクを高めます。品質表示と安全期限の混同も廃棄につながります。表示改善や適量包装などを検証する必要があります。

paragraphs.en: The economics of food waste ultimately concerns coordination. Farmers cannot perfectly predict retailers' orders, retailers cannot fully anticipate consumers, and charities cannot always receive surplus immediately. Better contracts, shared forecasts, reliable cold chains, transparent data, and carefully designed incentives can reduce these mismatches. Yet every intervention uses resources, so success should be measured by net benefits rather than by the volume of activity alone. A sound strategy prevents avoidable losses first, redirects safe surplus when practical, and manages unavoidable waste responsibly. The aim is not zero waste at any cost. It is a food system that uses resources efficiently while remaining safe, affordable, and resilient.
paragraphs.zh: 食物浪費經濟學最終涉及協調。農民無法完美預測零售商訂單，零售商無法完全預知消費者需求，慈善機構也不一定能即時接收剩餘食品。更好的合約、共享預測、可靠冷鏈、透明資料與精心設計的誘因能減少錯配。但每項措施都耗資源，成功應按淨效益而非活動量衡量。良好策略先預防可避免損失，再於可行時轉送安全剩餘食品，並負責任處理不可避免的廢棄物。目標不是不惜代價達成零浪費，而是安全、可負擔、具韌性且有效利用資源的食品系統。
paragraphs.ja: 食品ロスの経済学は供給網全体の調整の問題です。契約、需要予測の共有、冷蔵物流、透明なデータが役立ちます。ただし対策にも費用がかかるため、活動量ではなく純便益を評価します。安全性と手頃な価格を守りつつ、避けられる損失を減らすことが目標です。
